label: text
text: [Marshal Louis Lyautey, soldier and administrator, was born at Nancy. He entered the cavalry and had a brilliant career in Indochina, Madagascar, and Africa. In 1912 he was appointed Resident-General in Morocco, and also Minister for Foreign Affairs. A gifted administrator, he succeeded in pacifying Morocco, and in promoting its agriculture and trade. During the war he was for a short time War Minister in M. Briand's Cabinet (1916-17), but was re-appointed to Morocco in 1917) made a Marshal of France in (1920), he is well known as a writer, and is member of the French Academy.]

text: A message from Fez states that ominous rainstorms are falling in the Taza region which, if pressaging the beginning of the rainy season, are likely to delay the maturity of the French plans for a considerable time.

label: text
text: The Msoun river overflowed temporarily dislocating telegraphic communication between Fez and Taza.

label: text
text: At present the Riffs are trying to occupy the centre of the stage and are counter attacking at several points. Sharpshooters are harrassing the French garrison at Bibane.

label: text
text: The French claim that they have not only repulsed the attacks but have succeeded in advancing slightly at a point in the eastern sector.

label: text
text: Marshal Petain is likely temporarily to assume the administrative in addition to the military direction of Morocco in succession to Marshal Lyautey whose resignation will be accepted by the Cabinet.

label: text
text: A message from Fez states that rain stopped military movements being resumed by Abdel Krim. Reinforcing troops unsuccessfully attempted to occupy several posts.

label: text
text: Abdel Krim threatens dire vengeance to the tribes which have submitted to the French after having anticipatedly beaten the Spaniards.

label: text

Sir,—Exercising — that's the word describing the noise the street cars make when turning the corner, out of Russell Street into Persicival Street. I said 'What for', to a car conductor one morning. His reply was "I think so; he no wanebee go out this morning." I don't think the cars themselves have the will to strike, and feel sure that greasing the rails would remedy the noise.
If "Soporific" lived anywhere near that district, he would have something to really keep him awake at 8 a.m. So how about trotting around to the manager of the Tramways Company and pursuing him to have the rails "Correctly Lubricated?"
Yours, etc.
CROAS-HKAD

The delegates who arrived to attend the Empire Press Conference were given a banquet by the Commonwealth Government at Parliament House to-night.
The Prime Ministers, Mr. Bruce, in a speech, declared that the gathering was the most significant ever held in that hall.

label: text
text: The results of the visit would be of the greatest value to the Empire, particularly Australia.

label: text
text: The Chinese delegation sent by Marshal Feng Yu-hsiung has arrived here to study political and economic conditions in the Soviet Republic.

label: text
text: The delegation, which is headed by General Sung Ping, Chief of the General Staff of Feng's army, includes also the Marshal's secretaries.

label: text
text: The delegation will probably remain a month and will then possibly visit Western Europe.

label: text
text: Two hundred Communists tried to demonstrate at the pier but they were dispersed by police on the occasion of the arrival of the forty British delegates of the inter-Parliamentary conference headed by Sir Robert Horne.

label: text
text: It has been definitely decided that the Security Pact Conference will meet at Locarno on October 5.

The "Kenilworth Castle" is sailing this afternoon. The docks are assuming their normal aspect.
The passengers and cargo of the "Walmer Castle," which is arriving this afternoon will be landed at the jetty instead of in lighters.

label: text
text: The “Windsor Castle” and “Kildonan Castle” have both sailed with their original crews. The “Kenilworth Castle” is now the only mail boat remaining.

label: text
text: Hitherto 382 seamen have been charged in connection with the shipping strike and sentenced. The “Orvieto,” which is regarded as a test ship, has arrived. Only five of her crew went ashore and conferred with the strike leaders.

label: text
text: A Chinese clerk who was walking in Queen's Road Central with two others, suddenly dropped in a faint near the China Dispensary at 1.90 this afternoon.

label: text
text: The Dispensary doctor was quickly summoned and brought the young man to consciousness. He was taken to the Dispensary and was later able to walk into a taxicab which conveyed him home.

text: A Chinese girl was knocked down and injured at Cheung Sha Wan as a motor car belonging to the Chung Mei Garage was passing the Chiu Ki shipyard.

label: text
text: The driver of the car in his statement to the Police said that two girls suddenly darted in front of his car, and before he could pull up one of them was struck on the face by the mudguard. He picked up the injured girl and took her in his car to the Kwong Wah Hospital, where she was detained.

label: text
text: The injured girl was the daughter of a boatman whose vessel was under repair at the shipyard.

label: text
text: Yesterday afternoon at the Marina Ground, Kowloon, a trial Hockey match was played between two teams of the Hongkong Hockey Club.

label: text
text: The Match was fairly well contested, although "Whites" captained by J. Lammert had the lead throughout the whole game, and eventually won by three goals to one. The late start made play towards the end very difficult owing to approaching darkness.

label: text
text: The match started with Whites pressing and after ten minutes' play, from a good forward movement Faers opened the score. The game then settled down to a very evenly contested match, neither side adding any further score before halftime. The second half opened with a brilliant rush by Vallack and Lammert, the latter netting, giving Whites an additional lead. This woke Colours up and they pressed hard with the result that they scored. Lammert, however, once more got going and put through another goal five minutes later. Lammert had the misfortune to lose a fine opportunity just before the end when after a fine run down, owing to the failing light, he just missed an open goal. The whistle blew shortly after.

text: Tokyo, September 28. — The "Jiji" reports that the police have discovered that the Soviet Labour Delegates handed Japanese Socialists $1,200,000 before coming to Japan but the police will neither confirm nor deny this statement. Most of those arrested during the visit of the delegation have been released but a few of the leaders are still being held pending further investigation.—Reuter.
